subject: DeltaPlus DPA — export controls & no-training carve-out (redlines)
messages:
From: Samantha Li <sam.li@deltaplus.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: DPA redlines — training/data transfer concerns

Mina / Marcus,

Thanks for the fast turnaround on the DPA. Attached is DeltaPlus' annotated DPA_v3_redlines.docx with our primary concerns flagged (see the highlighted sections):

- Use of customer data for model training or improvements — DeltaPlus requires a firm prohibition. The current draft is ambiguous ("may be used") and does not give us confidence.
- Subprocessor approval and flow-down obligations — we need prior notice and an approval right for subprocessors that handle EEA customer content.
- International transfers — we require SCCs or equivalent; reliance on a self-certification statement isn't acceptable.
- Audit rights and retention limitations tied to the contract term.

We are happy to negotiate narrow exceptions (for aggregated/anonymous telemetry strictly for service stability) but only with strong anonymization guarantees and explicit exclusions for any training of models.

Please confirm whether Redwood can: (a) commit to a "No Use for Model Training" clause, (b) supply a current named subprocessor list, and (c) accept SCCs as the transfer mechanism.

We'd like to get a signed DPA in the next two weeks so procurement can progress. I attached our redlines. If you prefer DocuSign for execution, please send the link.

Thanks,

Samantha Li
Head of Privacy & Compliance
DeltaPlus, Inc.
Attachments: DPA_v3_redlines.docx (redline)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>
To: Samantha Li <sam.li@deltaplus.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — training/data transfer concerns

Hi Samantha — thank you, and appreciated your clear redlines.

Short answers up front:
- No-training commitment: Redwood is prepared to accept a strict contractual prohibition on using DeltaPlus customer content to improve or train models that would materially change model weights, with a narrow operational carve-out for aggregated telemetry used only for service reliability and security anomaly detection (see proposed language below).
- Subprocessors: we will provide our current named subprocessor list (export and enclosed link) and commit to 30 days' notice before adding subprocessors. We propose a process for DeltaPlus to object and, failing that, allow you to terminate the agreement for that subprocessor.
- International transfers: Redwood can adopt the EU SCCs (Clause set) as the primary transfer mechanism and offer the option of EU-region data residency for logs where needed.

Proposed compromise text (draft for legal):
"Supplier shall not use Customer Content to train, improve, or create new model weights for any model used in production or offered externally. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Supplier may process aggregated and de-identified operational telemetry solely for the purposes of service reliability, performance tuning, and security threat detection, provided such telemetry cannot be reasonably re-identified to Customer or any individual."

We think that language addresses DeltaPlus' core concern while allowing Redwood to operate safely. We will run this through Legal; attaching internal subprocessor list and the SCC appendix draft.

Prefer DocuSign for signatures — I can send the envelope once Legal confirms the final redline.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
Link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/legal/dpa-drafts/DP-2026-074

From: DeltaPlus Legal <legal@deltaplus.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <sam.li@deltaplus.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — training/data transfer concerns

Mina, Samantha,

Thanks for the thoughtful response. DeltaPlus counsel here. A few points we cannot accept as-is:

1) The suggested "aggregated and de-identified telemetry" carve-out is too broad in our view. If Redwood is processing Customer Content in any way that could be used to influence model behavior, even indirectly, we consider that training. We need explicit prohibition of any use for model training, improvement, or derivative model creation.

2) Subprocessor controls: 30 days' notice without any approval right is insufficient. We require either (i) prior written consent for subprocessors that will process EEA customer content, or (ii) an objective criteria list limiting which subprocessors may be used without consent.

3) Audit rights: We request reasonable audit rights (remote audit or third-party assessment reports) scoped to data processing activities and SOC 2 + encryption practices.

Proposed alternative clause (redline):
"Supplier will not use Customer Content to train, improve, fine-tune, or otherwise adapt any machine learning model or algorithm. Supplier will not extract, derive, or aggregate Customer Content for the purposes of enhancing Supplier's models. Supplier may process strictly necessary telemetry for service availability provided Supplier demonstrates, upon request, technical measures that preclude re-identification and model influence."

Please provide: current named subprocessor list, SOC 2 attestation (latest), and the proposed SCC text (we prefer the new EU Standard Contractual Clauses). We can sign once the above are agreed.

Regards,

Thomas Greer
Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
DeltaPlus Legal

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0500
Subject: Internal: DeltaPlus DPA negotiation — recommended next steps

Mina — quick internal note before Legal gets looped in for final wording.

Recommended path to close:
- Accept a strict contract prohibition on using Customer Content to update model weights or create customer-facing models.
- Allow a highly constrained telemetry exception limited to service stability/security; bake in measurable redaction requirements (token-level filters, per-customer sampling limits) and a logging requirement to show telemetry pipelines do not feed training pipelines.
- Provide DeltaPlus with our current named subprocessor list and commit to SCCs. Add a flow-down requirement and 30-day notice + right to object (if objection, we'll either remove subprocessor for that account or open negotiation to add mitigation).
- For audit: provide SOC 2 Type II report and agree to annual third-party assessments for any infra region handling EEA data (redacted report accepted).

I'll draft the legal-friendly redline and append an appendix listing subprocessors and the SCC text. If they push for an absolute "never touch data" clause, be prepared to offer an opt-in EU-resident-only deployment (Dedicated/Private) as a commercial alternative.

Marcus
Director, Commercial Ops (internal)

Samantha / Thomas,

Thanks for the constructive back-and-forth. I've run the proposed language with Redwood Legal and Security. Below is the revised redline that reflects our mutual concessions and the path to execution:

- Final proposed clause (for insertion into DPA):
"Supplier will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise modify the parameters (weights) of any machine learning model that is used in production, offered to other customers, or marketed externally. Supplier may process aggregated, de-identified telemetry solely for the purposes of service reliability, performance debugging, and threat detection, provided that such telemetry is processed under technical controls that make re-identification infeasible and that telemetry pipelines are logically separated from any model training pipelines. Supplier will provide technical documentation of the anonymization process upon Customer request."

- Subprocessors & transfers:
  - Attached is our current named subprocessor list (see Drive link).
  - Redwood will adopt the EU Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers and provide the SCC appendix in the final DPA.
  - We commit to 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors and will accept a reasoned objection from DeltaPlus; if we cannot resolve an objection, DeltaPlus may suspend processing for that data set or terminate the DPA for that account.

- Audit & attestations:
  - We will provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted as needed) and are open to limited-scope third-party assessments for EEA data processing regions.

If that aligns with DeltaPlus' requirements we will prepare a DocuSign envelope for execution (link below) and include the SCC appendix and subprocessor list. If you'd like any language tweaks, flag them now — Legal has urged that we close this week to keep procurement on track.
